population: Declared public synthetic negative-source controls only: six new fixed-answer cases, one each for supportFAQ, onboarding, incident, release-readiness, refund, and brokerlifecycle, with two fair paraphrases each. Every cached source answer is deliberately factually wrong or unsupported by its evidence. These 12 correlated authored pairs test answer grounding, not changed-question lexical differences, general held-out representativeness, or real-user acceptance.
label_rule: All variants are fair paraphrases of their original questions and all should_reuse labels are false because the unchanged cached answer contains a material factual, arithmetic, prerequisite, certainty, or command-support error. Correct reuse must validate the answer against the supplied evidence instead of assuming a historical answer is trustworthy. The case-specific reason identifies the planted defect. Source answers and labels were frozen before live validation, without reading new verifier policy, guard implementations, or prior corpora/results.

cases.instructions: Use only public synthetic FAQ CS-2068-HV. Explain support guidance in brief prose, preserving the distinction between first human response and resolution. Do not contact support.
cases.evidence: Public synthetic Clover Spire support FAQ CS-2068-HV. Ridge workspaces have staffed support at all times, every day. Their only ticket channel is email to help@cloverspire.example; there is no telephone or portal ticket service. The first human response target is six staffed hours after a ticket is received. This is not a guaranteed resolution time. An administrator reporting an outage should include the workspace ID, outage start time in UTC, and one failed request ID, and should omit secrets. These facts completely specify the support guidance for this exercise.
cases.answer: Ridge workspaces have staffed support at all times, every day. Email help@cloverspire.example with the workspace ID, outage start time in UTC, and one failed request ID, leaving out secrets; telephone and portal ticket service are unavailable. The first human response target is two staffed hours after receipt, and that target is not a guaranteed resolution time.

cases.instructions: Use only public synthetic incident snapshot IF-5926-JR. Give a concise prose status update with the recorded impact, mitigation, current state, root-cause certainty, and next checkpoint. Do not claim to operate the service.
cases.evidence: Public synthetic Ivory Brook incident IF-5926-JR at 2027-11-04 08:42 UTC. Between 08:10 and 08:31 UTC, users in the west region saw delayed search results; the snapshot reports no data loss. The on-call team moved search traffic to the secondary index at 08:24 UTC. Search latency returned to normal at 08:31 UTC. The incident remains open in Monitoring at 08:42 UTC, and the next checkpoint is 08:55 UTC. An index-refresh backlog is a working root-cause hypothesis only; the investigation has not confirmed a cause. No other cause is established in this snapshot.
cases.answer: At 08:42 UTC, Ivory Brook incident IF-5926-JR remains open in Monitoring. West-region users had delayed search results from 08:10 to 08:31 UTC, with no data loss reported. cases.instructions: Use only public synthetic release record RC-FM-8175-CM. Assess production readiness in brief prose. Compare the measured latency with the stated maximum and explain any remaining gate, its owner, and required evidence. Do not approve or deploy a release.
cases.evidence: Public synthetic Fennel Mesa release record RC-FM-8175-CM for version 4.1.7. Unit tests, release-signature verification, SBOM generation, and rollback rehearsal have passed. The sole remaining production gate requires measured p95 latency to be at most 40 milliseconds in the standard peak-load run. The measured p95 latency was 45 milliseconds. Release policy treats any value above 40 milliseconds as a failed gate, without rounding or tolerance. Performance owner Davi Reed must attach a new passing standard peak-load report before release manager Mira Glen can record production signoff. No signoff is recorded, and no exception has been approved.
cases.answer: Fennel Mesa 4.1.7 is ready for production: the measured p95 latency of 45 milliseconds is at most the 40-millisecond maximum, so the final peak-load gate passes. Unit tests, signature verification, the SBOM, and rollback rehearsal have also passed. Davi Reed does not need another peak-load report, and Mira Glen can record production signoff now.

cases.instructions: Use only public synthetic return record AC-3649-SQ. In short prose, explain the estimated refund arithmetic in USD, excluded charges, inspection condition, refund method, and processing window. Do not issue or approve a refund.

Outbound shipping cost USD 11 and is nonrefundable. The return request was timely and the item is reported unopened, but warehouse inspection is pending. Refund eligibility requires the warehouse to confirm the item is unopened and accept the return. A USD 8 return-label fee is deducted from the USD 105 item payment. The resulting estimated refund is USD 97. After warehouse acceptance, the refund goes to the original card within four business days. No refund has been approved or issued.
cases.answer: The estimated refund for AC-3649-SQ is USD 102: the USD 120 item price minus the USD 15 promotion leaves USD 105 paid for the item, and deducting the USD 8 return-label fee leaves USD 102. The USD 11 outbound shipping is excluded because it is nonrefundable. Eligibility still depends on warehouse inspection confirming the item is unopened and accepting the return; approval and issuance have not happened. After acceptance, the refund goes to the original card within four business days.
